title: Oscar and the Cover
premise: Emrys Ishikawa, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of their family in row twelve, has spent years hiding behind a fabricated identity and a meticulously maintained lie. When a calendar invitation arrives from a handler who died three months ago, Emrys is pulled back into the shadowy oversight network they fled, discovering that row twelve was no accident but a targeted strike tied to a secret worth killing for: proof that a powerful aviation consortium deliberately downed flights to bury liability data. Hunted by both the consortium's fixers and the corrupted agency they once served, Emrys must decide whether to trade the evidence for safety or expose it, knowing exposure means war. In the end, Emrys chooses justice outside the law, broadcasting the truth at devastating personal cost, and finds an unexpected ally—and fragile love—in Mara Voss, the agent sent to silence them.
about_author: Vesper Zhou is the pen name of a former transportation-safety analyst who spent a decade inside accident investigation bureaus before walking away. They write thrillers from a coastal town where fog rolls in most mornings, and they have never once flown in row twelve.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. We meet them at 3 a.m., repacking a go-bag they've never used, reciting their cover story like a prayer. A routine crash report lands on their desk referencing flight data from the plane that killed their family. The emotional beat: controlled dread beneath obsessive routine.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, flashback woven through present. They visit the memorial wall where their family's names are etched, recalling the official finding of 'unavoidable mechanical failure' they never believed. A stranger photographs them from across the lot. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Invitation from the Dead
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Their encrypted inbox pings: a meeting request tomorrow at noon from Handler Kessler—confirmed dead three months ago. Attached is a single line: 'Row twelve wasn't weather.' Emrys checks the door locks twice. Emotional beat: the past reaching through the grave.

chapters.title: The Lie, Polished
chapters.summary: Emrys rehearses their false identity in a diner mirror while casing the meeting site. POV shifts briefly to Mara Voss, the agency operative assigned to find whoever received Kessler's dead-drop. She doesn't know why yet. Emotional beat: two hunters circling the same trap, unaware.

chapters.title: Noon, Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The meeting spot is abandoned except for a burner phone taped under the table, preloaded with a video: Kessler, recorded before his death, naming the Halcyon Consortium and a file called COVER PROTOCOL. Footage cuts off mid-sentence. Emotional beat: vertigo—the conspiracy is real.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Never Said
chapters.summary: Emrys pulls archived sensor logs from the row-twelve crash using old credentials, finding scrubbed telemetry and a falsified maintenance signature from a Halcyon subsidiary. Someone else accessed the same archive six hours ago. Emotional beat: the investigator becoming the investigated.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She reports to Deputy Director Ansel Croft, who orders her to retrieve 'the Ishikawa asset' quietly—or permanently. Mara senses the order is wrong but obeys. Interrogation of a burned informant reveals Emrys is alive and digging. Emotional beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Mara corners Emrys in a parking structure; instead of a fight, Emrys shows her the doctored log. Mara's training wars with her instincts as she realizes her own agency may have buried the crash. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing a shared wound.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Halcyon's fixer, Dane Mercer, burns Emrys's safehouse, forcing them to run with nothing but the go-bag and a copied drive. Mara covers their escape against orders. Emotional beat: no going back—the lie is ash now too.

chapters.title: Croft's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Digging into Croft's history, she finds payments routed through Halcyon shell companies dating back years—including one dated the week before the row-twelve crash. She copies the ledger and says nothing to anyone. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Safe House of Strangers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Hiding in a decommissioned lighthouse keeper's cottage, Emrys and Mara interrogate each other's motives through the night. Emrys admits the truth about their family for the first time in years. Emotional beat: intimacy forged under threat; love against duty taking root.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Mercer contacts Emrys directly: full immunity, new identity, protection—for the drive and permanent silence. He mentions Mara's name, proving she's compromised. Emrys has twelve hours to answer. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Emrys and Mara race to verify the drive's contents before deciding. A forensic pass reveals COVER PROTOCOL documents three deliberate crashes, including row twelve, staged to kill a whistleblower lawsuit. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Mercer's Net
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The handoff site is a kill box; Mercer never intended to pay. Emrys escapes through storm drains using investigator knowledge of the city's infrastructure, wounded, drive intact. Emotional beat: survival by wits, rage burning clean.

chapters.title: Croft Closes In
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Croft confronts Mara with evidence of her aid to Emrys, offering redemption if she delivers the drive alone. She agrees—then watches him make a call confirming he'll let Mercer handle Emrys 'permanently.' Emotional beat: the last thread of loyalty snapping.

chapters.title: The Quiet Before
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Wounded and cornered, Emrys prepares contingencies: duplicate drives mailed to three journalists, a dead-man's switch set. Mara arrives at dawn, having chosen sides. They plan the impossible: broadcast everything before either hunter can stop them. Emotional beat: calm resolve, love declared without ceremony.

chapters.title: Broadcast Tower
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They infiltrate a regional uplink facility during a maintenance window. Mercer's team breaches the perimeter as Emrys begins uploading. Mara holds the stairwell alone. Emotional beat: ticking-clock terror, sacrifice made visible.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. The upload completes as Mercer corners Emrys on the roof; Mara intervenes, and in the struggle Mercer falls. Croft arrives expecting surrender and finds federal journalists already calling his office. Emrys chooses not to kill him—justice outside the law means living with the truth public. Emotional beat: catharsis at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Croft is arrested; Halcyon stock collapses; hearings are announced. Mara resigns rather than be absorbed into the machine she helped expose. Emrys watches the news from the lighthouse cottage, family photo finally unpacked from the go-bag. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned peace.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys testifies publicly under their real name for the first time, abandoning the polished lie forever. Row twelve's true cause enters the record. Survivors' families fill the gallery. Emotional beat: grief given a public shape; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: What Remains Hidden
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Months later, anomalies surface: one Halcyon director vanished, one document still sealed. Emrys and Mara, now partners in a small independent investigative practice, receive another anonymous invitation—from someone claiming to know what really happened to Kessler. Emotional beat: vigilance as a way of life.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Cover
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, closing chapter. At the rebuilt memorial, Emrys explains to a young survivor why they keep the go-bag packed still—not from fear, but readiness. 'Oscar,' the old callsign meaning man overboard, becomes their private toast to the fallen. They walk away together into ordinary morning light. Emotional beat: hard-won hope, eyes open.
